engine.notes: A small scene anchored by Big Couch since The New Movement closed; Two Friends and Anubis are the other teaching options, while Chris Trew's New Orleans School of Comedy Arts still advertises classes on social media but its website has not been updated since 2022.

entries.name: Big Couch New Orleans
entries.summary: Improv-rooted creative incubator with its own theater and bar at 1045 Desire St: a free four-week Improv 101, three further levels, sketch writing, a free Saturday jam and several improv shows a week.
entries.schedule: Shows most Wed-Sun evenings; free improv jam Saturdays 1-2 pm; Improv 101 is free, 201-401 run eight weeks
signals: Own theater and bar in Bywater
October 2026 calendar lists ten improv shows
entries.reasons: A permanent home, a ladder from a free 101 to forms work, a weekly jam and a busy October 2026 calendar, held back only by its youth and a thinner reputation than older theaters elsewhere.

entries.name: Two Friends Improv Theater
entries.summary: Four-level improv school and monthly show company resident at The Actor's Apothecary on Prytania Street; six-week evening courses with scholarships for women, people of color and LGBTQ students.
entries.schedule: Shows first Wednesday and third Saturday monthly at 8 pm; Level 1 starts Monday Sept 28, 2026 ($160, six weeks)
signals: Resident at The Actor's Apothecary, 1506 Prytania St
entries.reasons: A clear four-level path and a dependable two-shows-a-month rhythm, but no venue of its own, no house teams and only a handful of show dates a year.

entries.name: Anubis Improv
entries.summary: Long-form improv school founded in 2018 by David James Hamilton, teaching a four-level, eight-week curriculum that ends in a showcase, with shows in New Orleans and a second branch in Oxford, Mississippi.
entries.schedule: Each level runs eight weeks and ends in a live showcase; show dates go out by newsletter
signals: Eight-week levels end in a showcase
entries.reasons: A structured long-form curriculum from an experienced teacher, but no theater of its own, no public show calendar on the site and a schedule you have to join a newsletter to see.
